items.name: WSimpleZone::IsZoneInRange

Bodies are identical: 1<<n bias on the x/y/z differences, OR'd, then >>(n+1)==0. Xbox sits just before WSimpleZone::SetPosition.

items.name: InputTable::~InputTable

items.name: EAGL::Model::MorphModel
evidence: Version Tracking candidate, body review: EAGL::Model::Call: Xbox inlines strcmp(name,'Morph') then calls ea480, and PS2 Call calls MorphModel on 'Morph'. Both walk the +0xd4 morph table, match names against the +0xb8 list, decode bits 0x1c/0x1e of the header with a 0xfffffff length, dst = [2]*(+0xc0)+[3], and dispatch to 3 per-type morph routines.

items.name: EAGL::Model::ClearMorphModel
evidence: on the caller chain of EAGL::Model::MorphModel, body review: Model::Call's 'ClearMorph' branch on both. It walks the +0xb8 list and copies n=(short)*(hw>>1) bytes from dst-off to dst, or to dst+off*(+0xc0) if bit 1 is set. It is the PS2 memcpy loop, inlined as rep movs on Xbox.

items.name: PBondCar::GlareOff
evidence: Version Tracking candidate, body review: Called twice (3,4) at the start of 0x62de0 and from Simulate, the same as PS2 GlareOff from HandleTurnSignals/Simulate. It mirrors the named Xbox GlareOn: if state[i]==1, virtual call (2, 1<<(i+0x10), 0, g, g, -1.0) then (0xc, i, ...), state=0. GlareOn uses 0 and 0xb.

items.name: PBondCar::HandleTurnSignals
evidence: Version Tracking candidate, body review: Called from PBondCar::Simulate on both. GlareOff(3), GlareOff(4); signal state (PS2 +0x39c, Xbox +0x390) 1/2 compares +0x398/+0x240 (Xbox +0x38c/+0x240) and clears; blink = (frame - start) % period > period*(1-duty); then virtual GlareOn(3 or 4). Offsets are shifted -0xc consistently.

items.name: RCMP::AV_PLAYER::IsTimeForDecode
evidence: on the caller chain of RCMP::DECODER::GetFrameRate, body review: Called only from PlayMPC::Play on both. Body: audio time + [0x40], times GetFrameRate()*0.001, stored at +0x48, return (float)[0x44]+1.0 <= that. Offsets are identical.

items.name: EAGL::RuntimeAllocConstructorPool::~RuntimeAllocConstructorPool
evidence: Version Tracking candidate, body review: The atexit stub 0x15d150 calls it with ECX=0x23fbb8. That global is used by Xbox DynamicLoader::Resolve (with RuntimeAllocConstructorPool::FindConstructor/Destructor), matching PS2 0x348b28, which PS2 _global_ctor_dtor destroys with ~RuntimeAllocConstructorPool. Body: ~SymbolPool on this, this+0x14, this+0x14, this, exactly like PS2. There is no delete flag, so it is the plain destructor. It also sits in the PS2 slot between ConstructorPool::FindDestructor and RuntimeAllocConstructorPool::RemoveType.
PS2 0x29e1f8

items.name: EAGL::ConstructorPool::~ConstructorPool

items.name: EAGL::SymbolPool::~SymbolPool
